repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: Canonical, maintainer-authored documentation lives in docs/wiki/ — treat it as the primary source of truth and mirror its organization. The intended navigation is defined in docs/wiki/_sidebar.md. Each docs/wiki/*.md file and subdirectory (architecture/, tools/, configuration/, guidelines/, code-generation/, diagnostics/, security/) maps to a wiki section. Prefer the framing, terminology, and grouping used there over inferring structure from the source layout alone. README.md and SKILL.md are secondary narrative sources; src/ is the source of truth for behavior.

repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: Inventory counts change every release, so do NOT hardcode them in the wiki. Whenever a count is needed, derive it from source at documentation-generation time rather than stating a fixed number, and prefer describing the categories over enumerating totals. Counting method (source of truth): MCP tools = #[McpTool] attributes across src/Mcp/Tool/*.php, split into tier-1 (visible in tools/list at startup) and tier-2 (hidden but callable by name and discoverable via search-tools); MCP resources = #[McpResource] in src/Mcp/Resource; MCP prompts = #[McpPrompt] in src/Mcp/Prompt; development guidelines = files under config/guidelines/; skill guides = files under config/skills/. When a number must appear, phrase it as a derived snapshot (e.g. 'the MCP tools — currently <N>, see src/Mcp/Tool/'), never as a fixed promise, and never write approximations like '80+'.

repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: Core terminology — use this exact phrasing. The workflow is 'check → learn → write' (lowercase, with arrows); do NOT rename it 'Check-Learn-Write'. It means: check runtime state via introspection tools (check-class, eav-attributes, diagnose-error, etc.) → load domain guidelines via development-context → then write code. The guiding principle is 'runtime-first': Magento resolves DI, plugins, preferences, and events at runtime across all installed modules, so reading source files alone misses cross-module overrides, conflicts, and customizations. Bricklayer exists to close that gap.

repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: Tools are organized along two axes. Visibility (progressive disclosure): tier-1 tools appear in tools/list at startup (a small curated set); tier-2 tools are omitted from the list but callable by name and surfaced via search-tools (the majority) — this reduces token overhead while keeping every tool callable. Do not hardcode the per-tier counts; derive them from source if a number is needed. Safety: read-only tools only require an initialized Magento (requireMagento) with no config gate; destructive tools (delete, refund, code generation, code-runner with writes) additionally require non-production (requireNonProduction) and ship disabled by default via ConfigInitializer::DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS (enabled:false). code-runner defaults to read-only with its DB transaction rolled back unless allow_write is set.

repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: Scope and positioning: Bricklayer is a Composer library that runs an MCP server for Magento 2 — it is NOT a Magento module and installs nothing into app/code. It supports a range of Magento 2.4.x and PHP 8.x versions — read the constraints in composer.json for the current supported range instead of citing fixed versions. It auto-detects and supports Native, DDEV, Warden, and Docker environments (entrypoints bin/bricklayer-mcp and bin/bricklayer-mcp-docker; src/Integration/McpConfigWriter.php generates the correct exec command per environment). Multi-agent support: Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, JetBrains AI, and Gemini CLI. The name reflects laying components ('bricks') in the correct order to build a maintainable codebase. License: MIT. For the authoritative supported Magento/PHP version ranges, read the require/require-dev constraints in composer.json rather than restating fixed numbers here.

repo_notes.author: Bricklayer maintainers
repo_notes.content: This repository is the Bricklayer toolkit itself (PSR-4 autoload Inchoo\\MagentoBricklayer\\ under src/, tests under tests/). Do NOT document any surrounding example Magento project, vendor/, or generated/ output that may exist in a host installation — only this package. The 'June 2026' commit and copyright dates are correct and intentional; do not treat them as data errors. Do not pin the wiki to a specific package version — omit version-specific statements so the documentation stays valid across releases; if a version is ever needed, read it from composer.json or the latest git tag at generation time.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to Bricklayer: what it is (a Composer library exposing an MCP server for Magento 2), the runtime-first problem it solves (agents reading source files miss cross-module DI/plugin/preference/event overrides), and headline capabilities. Mirror docs/wiki/home.md and README.md sections 'What is Bricklayer?' and 'How Agents Use Bricklayer'. Describe the capability set (MCP tools, resources, prompts, development guidelines, and skill guides) without hardcoding totals — derive any count from source at generation time — and the check → learn → write workflow.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Landing page for new users: requirements (supported Magento 2.4.x / PHP 8.x range — cite composer.json constraints rather than fixed numbers), installation paths, and first steps. Mirror docs/wiki/getting-started.md and README 'Requirements' / 'Installation' / 'Quick Start'. Acts as parent for the detailed installation, developer-guide, and FAQ pages.

pages.title: Installation & Setup
pages.purpose: Step-by-step installation: composer require inchoo/magento-bricklayer as a dev dependency vs global install; running 'bricklayer install' to generate agent and MCP client config; 'bricklayer init' to scaffold project-local overrides. Source: src/Command/InstallCommand.php, src/Command/InitCommand.php, src/Integration/McpConfigWriter.php; docs/wiki/getting-started.md.

pages.title: Developer Guide
pages.purpose: Practical end-to-end guide to using Bricklayer with an AI agent: the check → learn → write loop, when to reach for which tool, and worked examples grounded in real tools (check-class before a plugin, eav-attributes before touching product/customer data, diagnose-error when debugging, development-context before writing code). Mirror docs/wiki/developer-guide.md.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.purpose: Common questions and troubleshooting. Mirror docs/wiki/faq.md. Cover production-mode behavior and disabled destructive tools, why most tools are hidden at startup (progressive disclosure / search-tools), and container-detection issues.

pages.title: Key Concepts and Terminology
pages.purpose: Foundational concepts and glossary on one page: the runtime-first principle, the check → learn → write workflow, tool visibility tiers (tier-1 visible / tier-2 hidden), tool safety classes (read-only vs destructive), progressive disclosure, MCP primitives (tools/resources/prompts), guidelines vs skills, and development-context categories. Define each term exactly as used in src/ and SKILL.md.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: System architecture overview: how the Composer library boots Magento, builds the MCP server, registers tools, and serves resources/prompts. Mirror docs/wiki/architecture/overview.md. Parent for the bootstrap, server/registry, and resources/prompts pages.

pages.title: MCP Tools Reference
pages.purpose: Index of all MCP tools grouped by domain, with the tier-1/tier-2 visibility split (a small set visible at startup, the rest discoverable via search-tools) and the read-only vs destructive classification. Do not hardcode totals — derive any count from src/Mcp/Tool/ at generation time. Mirror docs/wiki/tools/overview.md. Parent for the per-domain tool pages below.

pages.title: Introspection Tools
pages.purpose: Runtime introspection tools — the core of the 'check' step: check-class, di-configuration, plugin-list, preference-list, event-list, module-list/module-structure, eav-attributes/eav-entity-types, and route/api/url-rewrite tools. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/{ApplicationTools,ModuleTools,EavTools,RoutingTools,DevelopmentTools}.php; docs/wiki/tools/introspection.md.

pages.title: Catalog, Order, and Customer Tools
pages.purpose: Service-layer CRUD over catalog, sales, and customers, plus batch execution. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/{CatalogTools,OrderTools,CustomerTools,BatchTools}.php; docs/wiki/tools/{catalog,orders,customers}.md. Note which operations are destructive (create/update/delete, invoice/credit-memo/refund) and ship disabled in production.

pages.title: Database and Log Tools
pages.purpose: Direct database schema/query inspection and log reading/searching. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/{DatabaseTools,LogTools}.php; docs/wiki/tools/{database,logs-and-diagnostics}.md. Cover read-only query safeguards and log-output controls (e.g. max_entry_length).

pages.title: Diagnostic and Performance Tools
pages.purpose: diagnose-error (exception log + stack trace + DI context + plugin-chain analysis + fix suggestions in one call), diagnose-performance (indexes, cache, cron, query patterns), system-status, and application-info. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/{DiagnosticTools,PerformanceTools,Diagnostic/*}.php; docs/wiki/diagnostics/overview.md.

pages.title: GraphQL Tools
pages.purpose: GraphQL schema introspection — types, queries, mutations, and resolvers. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/GraphqlTools.php; docs/wiki/tools/graphql.md.

pages.title: Code Runner Tool
pages.purpose: code-runner: execute multi-step PHP against the booted Magento application in a single call, with helper functions (repo(), etc., documented by code-runner-help). Read-only by default with the DB transaction rolled back; writes require allow_write. Document its security model. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/CodeRunnerTools.php.

pages.title: Code Generation Tools
pages.purpose: Scaffolding generators — generate-module, generate-model, generate-controller, generate-api — and the MCP prompt templates that drive them, with conflict detection and Magento-compliant output. Destructive (writes files), disabled in production. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/CodeGenerationTools.php, src/Mcp/Prompt/*; docs/wiki/code-generation/overview.md.

pages.title: Development and System Tools
pages.purpose: Agent-workflow and system tools: development-context (load guidelines by category), search-tools (discover hidden tier-2 tools), search-docs, configuration-get/list, and reinitialize. Source: src/Mcp/Tool/{ContextTools,SearchTools,ConfigurationTools,DevelopmentTools}.php; docs/wiki/tools/development.md.

pages.title: Guidelines and Skills System
pages.purpose: The development guidelines (config/guidelines/: core, patterns, modules, areas, database, ecosystem) and skill guides (config/skills/) — describe the categories, not a fixed count — how development-context categories map to them, and how they are compiled, served, and overridden. Source: src/Guidelines/GuidelinesCompiler.php, src/Mcp/Resource/{GuidelinesResource,SkillsResource,CodingStandardsResource}.php; docs/wiki/guidelines/overview.md.

pages.title: Security Model
pages.purpose: Production safety and code-execution security: deploy-mode-aware defaults, requireNonProduction gating, DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS disabled-by-default, code-runner read-only/transaction-rollback behavior, and database-query protections. Source: src/Config/ConfigInitializer.php, src/Mcp/Tool/CodeRunnerTools.php; docs/wiki/security/overview.md; SECURITY.md.
